content: Acetaminophen oral solution is an analgesic and antipyretic medication approved by the FDA for the treatment of minor aches and pains, including those caused by headaches, muscle aches, and backaches. It is also used to temporarily reduce fever. Common side effects include itching, constipation, nausea, vomiting, headache, agitation, insomnia, and atelectasis. Adult Indications and Dosage: Acetaminophen oral solution is indicated for the temporary relief of minor aches and pains due to headaches, muscle aches, backaches, minor arthritis pain, the common cold, toothaches, and premenstrual or menstrual cramps. It is also used to temporarily reduce fever. Adults should not exceed the recommended dosage. Taking more than six doses in 24 hours can lead to severe liver damage. Off-Label Use: There is limited information available regarding off-label uses of acetaminophen oral solution in adults, whether supported by guidelines or not. Pediatric Indications and Dosage: There is limited information regarding FDA-labeled or off-label uses of acetaminophen oral solution in pediatric patients. Contraindications: There is limited information regarding contraindications for pediatric patients. However, acetaminophen should not be used in individuals allergic to it or any of its inactive ingredients. Warnings: Liver Warning: Severe liver damage may occur if an adult takes more than six doses in 24 hours, a child takes more than five doses in 24 hours, or an adult consumes three or more alcoholic drinks daily while using this product. Sore Throat Warning: If a sore throat is severe, persists for more than two days, or is accompanied by fever, headache, rash, nausea, or vomiting, consult a doctor promptly. Do not use acetaminophen with any other drug containing acetaminophen (prescription or non-prescription). If unsure, consult a doctor or pharmacist. Consult a doctor before use if the user has liver disease or is taking the blood-thinning drug warfarin. Stop use and consult a doctor if pain worsens or lasts more than 10 days in adults, more than five days in children under 12, or if fever worsens or lasts more than three days. New symptoms, redness, or swelling may indicate a serious condition. Adverse Reactions: There is limited information regarding clinical trial and post-marketing experiences with acetaminophen oral solution. Drug Interactions: There is limited information regarding drug interactions with acetaminophen oral solution. Use in Specific Populations: Pregnancy: Acetaminophen is classified as Pregnancy Category C by the FDA. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should consult a healthcare professional before use. Labor and Delivery: There is no FDA guidance on the use of acetaminophen during labor and delivery. Nursing Mothers: There is no FDA guidance on the use of acetaminophen in nursing mothers. Pediatric Use: Keep out of reach of children. Geriatric Use: There is no FDA guidance on the use of acetaminophen in geriatric patients. Gender, Race, Renal Impairment, Hepatic Impairment, and Immunocompromised Patients: There is no specific FDA guidance on the use of acetaminophen in these populations. Administration and Monitoring: Acetaminophen oral solution is administered orally. There is limited information regarding monitoring requirements for this medication. Overdosage: Taking more than the recommended dose can cause liver damage. In case of overdose, seek medical help or contact a Poison Control Center immediately (1-800-222-1222). Prompt medical attention is critical, even if no symptoms are present. Pharmacology: There is limited information regarding the mechanism of action, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology of acetaminophen oral solution. Storage: Store at 20°C to 25°C (68°F to 77°F). Precautions with Alcohol: The interaction between alcohol and acetaminophen oral solution has not been established. Consult a doctor about the effects of consuming alcohol while taking this medication. Brand Names: Acetaminophen Oral Solution USP. Look-Alike Drug Names: There is limited information regarding look-alike drug names for acetaminophen oral solution.
